quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: To enter a gap in highway traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and let the other vehicles make way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before you change lanes or enter traffic, check behind and beside your vehicle. Make sure no vehicles are in the lane you want to enter.

questions.question: If you are driving on a highway next to a single broken white line, what can you do?

options.text: You cannot cross the line to pass.
You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You can cross a dashed white line to pass or change lanes if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, which lane should you start from?

options.text: Any lane (as long as it is safe).
The lane closest to the left curb.
The lane in the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street to another one-way street, start your turn from the far left lane.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Side road.
Merge.
Yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Side road.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a side road intersection is ahead.

questions.question: A reflective orange triangle on the back of a vehicle means:

options.text: It is a slow-moving vehicle.
It is an ambulance.
It is a school bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: A reflective orange triangle on a vehicle's back means it travels 25 mph or slower. You may see this on farm equipment, construction vehicles, or horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: Strong wind gusts on highways can:

options.text: Generally affect only the movement of large vehicles.
Only cause visibility problems.
Cause problems for all vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cause problems for all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Wind affects all drivers, not just large vehicles. Wind can reduce visibility by blowing dust and dirt, and it can also push vehicles off course.

questions.question: At an intersection with a yield sign, you must:

options.text: Yield to cross traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.
Yield to vehicles only on your right.
Slow down but never stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to cross traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, give the right-of-way to traffic in the lanes you plan to enter or cross. Be ready to stop if needed, but you can go if no traffic is coming.

questions.question: This sign warns drivers that:

options.text: The right lane is ending and traffic should merge left.
The road curves ahead.
There are upcoming intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane is ending and traffic should merge left.
questions.explanation: This yellow sign warns you that a lane is ending. Traffic must merge left ahead.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?

options.text: They do not follow the same rules as motor vehicles.
A motorcycle can stop much faster than a standard vehicle.
They brake more slowly than motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle can stop much faster than a standard vehicle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles stop quickly. If you follow too closely and the rider stops suddenly, you will not have enough time to stop. Keep extra space between you and motorcycles.

questions.question: Use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days so that:

options.text: You can keep your engine warm.
Other drivers can see your vehicle.
You can warn others of bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Other drivers can see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: On rainy, snowy, or foggy days, other drivers have trouble seeing your vehicle. Turn on your headlights to make your vehicle easier to see. If you use your windshield wipers, you must also turn on your low beam headlights.

questions.question: "No zones" are areas around trucks where cars:

options.text: Cannot be seen by the driver or are too close for the driver to stop and turn safely.
Have enough space to travel behind the truck.
Have several car lengths between them and the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot be seen by the driver or are too close for the driver to stop and turn safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are blind spot areas around trucks or buses where cars cannot be seen. They are also areas where cars are so close that the truck or bus driver cannot stop or turn safely. A car in a "No zone" greatly increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: When parking next to a curb, you should use your turn signals:

options.text: Only when leaving the curb.
When moving toward the curb, but not when leaving it.
When moving toward or leaving the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When moving toward or leaving the curb.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal both when parking next to a curb and when leaving it.

questions.question: Allow extra space in front of your vehicle when following a:

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger vehicle.
Motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space when following a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop faster than cars. You need room to stop if the rider brakes suddenly or falls. Also, motorcycles are hard to see at night because they have only one tail light.

questions.question: Crosswalks are:

options.text: Always marked with pavement lines.
Marked with lines or unmarked.
Never marked with lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: Marked with lines or unmarked.
questions.explanation: Crosswalks exist whether they are marked or not. You must stop for pedestrians at any crosswalk.

questions.question: When driving in a construction zone:

options.text: Speed up slightly.
Be ready for anything to happen.
Expect construction workers to move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for anything to happen.
questions.explanation: Construction zones have unexpected conditions. Drive very carefully for your safety, the safety of other drivers, and the safety of construction workers.

questions.question: Stopping distances and the severity of collisions:

options.text: Get shorter as you drive faster.
Are not affected by how fast you drive.
Get longer as you drive faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get longer as you drive faster.
questions.explanation: Speeding is dangerous. Higher speeds increase stopping distance and make crashes worse, causing more injuries and deaths. Keep more distance between your car and the car ahead when you drive faster.

questions.question: If you experience a tire blowout:

options.text: Tap or pump the brakes.
Slow down gradually and use light braking.
Brake hard and fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and use light braking.
questions.explanation: If you have a tire blowout, lift your foot off the gas pedal slowly. Do not brake hard until your speed drops significantly.

questions.question: How should drivers apply the gas pedal?

options.text: Slowly and smoothly
As fast as possible
By tapping lightly

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly and smoothly
questions.explanation: Press the gas pedal slowly and smoothly. Pressing too hard too fast can make your wheels spin, making your car hard to control.

questions.question: Construction zone signs are usually:

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red colors.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow colors.
Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black colors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black colors.
questions.explanation: All temporary work zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols. These signs are on the right side of the road, or on both sides on divided highways.

questions.question: When you have a green light and pedestrians are in the intersection:

options.text: You must let pedestrians cross first.
You have the right-of-way over pedestrians.
Pedestrians must wait for you to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: When you have a green light, you must let pedestrians and other vehicles already in the intersection cross first. Always yield to pedestrians when turning on a green light.

questions.question: Which road surface freezes first?

options.text: A tunnel
An intersection
A bridge

questions.correctAnswerText: A bridge
questions.explanation: Bridge surfaces freeze before other road surfaces. They freeze first and thaw last.

questions.question: What color are traffic control devices in construction and work areas?

options.text: Red.
Orange.
Yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange.
questions.explanation: Orange signs, cones, and barriers mark work zones. Drive with extra caution when you see orange warning devices.

questions.question: What does this yellow sign mean?

options.text: One lane ahead.
Merging traffic ahead.
Lane ends ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merging traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic may merge into your lane ahead.

questions.question: You are parked downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parked downhill without a curb, turn your wheels right toward the road edge. If your brakes fail, the car will roll away from traffic. When parked uphill without a curb, turn your wheels left toward the center so the car rolls into the curb.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection with a steady yellow light and have not entered it yet. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Come to a safe stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a safe stop.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection, clear it quickly.
